data.title: Operational Infrastructure Concealed Behind Intermediaries
data.summary:
Campaign infrastructure — domains, hosting and accounts — is registered through privacy
services, resellers and intermediaries that break the link between the assets and any
operator.
data.description:
Concealment is routine rather than remarkable, and its presence is weak evidence of
sophistication: privacy registration is the default at most registrars. What carries
weight is concealment that is inconsistent or incomplete — one asset in a cluster
registered openly, a reused registrant email, infrastructure that predates the privacy
service.

Those inconsistencies are where attribution actually comes from, and they are usually
found by looking at the cluster rather than at the best-hidden member of it.

The report should be explicit that concealment limits attribution rather than implying
anything about who is behind it. Operators conceal infrastructure; so do ordinary people
with ordinary privacy preferences.
data.recommendation:
* Preserve registration and hosting records at the time of observation; they change and
  historical records are not always retrievable.
* Pursue the inconsistent assets in a cluster rather than the best-concealed one.
* State plainly where concealment prevents attribution rather than filling the gap with
  inference.
data.short_recommendation: Preserve registration records; attribute from the cluster's inconsistencies.
